column1: # xfrm_audit.tsv -- KNOWN data-plane defects, declared at their exact value.
# Every live row is audited by xfrm_audit.sh (ICV length, packet counters,
# per-SA integrity failures, /proc/net/xfrm_stat error counters).  A row
# listed here is XFAIL for that check; when the defect is fixed the audit
# reports XPASS and FAILS the row so the entry has to be deleted.
#          stat  (value: Counter=N[,Counter=N]  -- may rise by at most N)

column4: RFC 5685 drain row: drain-sa SET deliberately tears down the established Child SA (R esp 2 to 0) and REDIRECTs the peer to a sibling, so NO live traffic remains at row end by design.  The flat post-drain counters are the PASS condition, not a defect; the row gate asserts teardown + redirect on the wire.

RFC 5685 two-gateway redirect row: the child selector is a /24-subnet (192.0.30.0/24 served by both gateways); only the child SAs are keyed by the redirect flow, and the harness's generic host-to-host (/32) xa_probe does not cover /24-subnet children, so no data-plane traffic is expected at row end.  The row's gates are the failover-landing: initiator wire re-target to the LIVE sibling C + C and I both holding keyed ESP child SAs (esp>=2) while draining A stays at 0.  That is the proof; data-plane traversal of the subnet child is explicitly out of scope for this landing row.

RFC 5685 drain refuses ticketed resume row: after the drained responder NACKs the ticketed IKE_SESSION_RESUME (38), the initiator's fallback likely re-drives IKE_SA_INIT toward the drain gateway (192.0.99.7, unreachable in this 2-seat row) so no child is installed at row end — the row's proof is the REFUSAL (drain-NACK sent, resume NOT accepted) + initiator fallback, not a live data plane.  Declared traffic XFAIL by design; the kind asserts the refusal + fallback itself.
